title: AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon
titleZh: AMD 收购 Taalas，通过在硅中蚀刻模型来提高推理性能
author: itvision
relevanceReason: 命中 4 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: In AMD’s latest bid to upset Nvidia's dominance in AI hardware, the House of Zen has acquired AI chip company Taalas, which bakes model weights directly into silicon in a process that promises to boost inference performance by an order of magnitude or more.The deal, announced at market close on Thursday, appears to be framed in much the same context as Nvidia’s $20 billion licensing deal with Groq last December: make high-performance “premium” inference services prized for AI agents, like code assistants, faster and cheaper to run. AMD didn’t disclose the terms of the deal, but from what we understand, this is an actual acquisition rather than an acquihire.Founded in 2023 and based in Toronto, Taalas’ approach to inference is radically different from conventional GPUs or the dataflow architectures that underpin Groq LPUs or Cerebras' waferscale accelerators.

The startup’s chips don’t rely on HBM to store the model weights but rather etch them directly into the silicon. In a sense, Taalas’ chips are really model-specific integrated circuits or MSICs.Perhaps more importantly, Taalas’ tech isn’t just conceptual. In February, the startup revealed its first test chip fabbed on TSMC’s 6nm process tech, which it called the HC1. Initial benchmarks saw the chip serve Meta’s Llama 3.1 8B at a blistering 16,960 tokens a second — when announced last February, that was 48x faster than Nvidia's GPUs and 8.5x faster than Cerebras' accelerators. While Llama 3.1 is ancient by today’s standards, having made its debut all the way back in mid 2024, the reticle-sized chip was really intended to prove the concept. Taalas has been incredibly secretive about how its chips actually work, but we know its processors are comprised of two main regions: the mask-ROM recall fabric where model weights are etched, and the SRAM recall fabric where KV caches and fine-tuning adapters are stored.For its second-gen HC2 chip due out this summer, Taalas aims to boost parameter count to 20 billion parameters. That might not sound like much, but just like with GPUs for larger models, weights are simply distributed across multiple accelerators using pipeline parallelism.At 20 billion parameters per chip, you’d need just 50 accelerators to support a trillion-parameter model, and AMD just so happens to have a rack-scale compute platform and in-house system design team that can comfortably accommodate that.That’s quite a bit more space and power efficient than Nvidia’s recently unveiled LPX systems, which would need a few dozen GPUs and at least 2,000 Groq LPUs to serve the same model.From what we understand, AMD intends to pair its Instinct-based Helios racks with chips based on Taalas’ tech, which implies a disaggregated architecture where compute-heavy prompt processing is done on GPUs while token generation is offloaded to Taalas-based accelerators.

comments.author: TechTechTech
comments.textRawHtml:
I think what will happen is what happened to something like 4K video decoding before where it ends up in silicon costing almost nothing to run extremely fast on device.

"Good enough" LLM functionality (for the use case) will be on-die or on-chip for cars, appliances, etc. This will provide speeds of chatjimmy at a battery-level power consumption.

Probably this will also happen for software engineering. Some usb-powered AI accelerator with Kimi K3 (and in future even better) performance running at 10K+ tokens/sec under 50W of power purchasable for almost no cost. Need a better model? Buy the new hardware. Old hardware is probably still fine for a lot of other use-cases. I expect China to be a big player here, it fits their open-model and hardware-manufacturing strategy.
comments.textZhHtml:
我认为将会发生的情况与之前 4K 视频解码之类的事情一样，它最终会在芯片上几乎不需要花费任何成本就可以在设备上运行得极快。

“足够好”的 LLM 功能（针对用例）将位于汽车、电器等的芯片上或芯片上。这将以电池级功耗提供 chatjimmy 的速度。

这可能也会发生在软件工程中。一些 USB 供电的 AI 加速器具有 Kimi K3（将来甚至更好）的性能，在 50W 功率下以 10K+ 代币/秒的速度运行，几乎可以免费购买。需要更好的模型吗？购买新硬件。旧硬件可能仍然适用于许多其他用例。我预计中国将成为这里的重要参与者，这符合他们的开放模式和硬件制造战略。

children.author: OneDeuxTriSeiGo
children.textRawHtml:
Assistive technology.

Imagine an energy efficient IC for a small multimodal model that can do voice to text, text to speech, question/answer, tool calling, and structured output.

Wire that up to a microcontroller that parses the structured output to constrain the model (rather than giving the model direct hardware access).

Now you have an assistive tech mode for supporting vision impaired users without requiring them to configure an app on their phone, pair devices, etc. And so now the user can just speak to the washing machine to tell it what to do.

And because models are getting better and better at multi-language support, you can rely on a single model to cover a wide range of spoken languages. And therefore you don't need a bunch of variants of this chip for a single product line.

TLDR this gives a path to replace "always online" and "wifi enabled" devices with fully on-device capabilities without being forced to abandon assistive technology support.
children.textZhHtml:
辅助技术。

想象一个用于小型多模式模型的节能 IC，可以执行语音转文本、文本转语音、问题/答案、工具调用和结构化输出。

将其连接到解析结构化输出以约束模型的微控制器（而不是为模型提供直接硬件访问）。

现在，您拥有一种辅助技术模式，可以支持视力受损的用户，而无需他们在上配置应用程序他们的手机、配对设备等。因此，现在用户只需对洗衣机说话，告诉它该做什么。

而且，由于模型在多语言支持方面越来越好，您可以依靠单个模型来涵盖广泛的口语。因此，您不需要为单个产品线提供该芯片的大量变体。

TLDR，这提供了一条用完全设备上功能替换“始终在线”和“启用 WiFi”设备的途径，而无需被迫放弃辅助技术支持。

children.author: mixermachine
children.textRawHtml:
Scaling a model on a chip is quite hard. ChatJimmy is based on Llama 3.1 8 billion. Kimi K3 has 2.8 trillion parameters. That are 350x more parameters.

I would expect that Gemma 4 E2B (approx 5.1 billion parameters) or maybe even Gemma 4 26 billion A4B at some point is running on a chip.
children.textZhHtml:
在芯片上扩展模型非常困难。 ChatJimmy 基于 Llama 3.1 8 亿。 Kimi K3有2.8万亿个参数。 参数数量增加了 350 倍。

我预计 Gemma 4 E2B（大约 51 亿个参数）甚至 Gemma 4 260 亿个 A4B 在某个时刻都在芯片上运行。

children.author: jermaustin1
children.textRawHtml:
I have found that for some personal prose-related projects, QWEN 3.6 35B A3B is an amazing model even quantized down to 4 bits. I actually find it's "writing" style as a GM for an LLM-powered solo text adventure game, better than even some of the faster/dummer frontier models like GPT-5.6-Luna or Haiku 4.5, and it runs (slowly) on a 3090 with a 80k context.

So I have faith in these embedded LLM chips when it comes to fun projects like that. I have not personally found my quantized QWEN good at agentic tasks, though, and it LOVES to make shit up when asking questions about documents in the prompt.
children.textZhHtml:
我发现对于一些个人散文相关的项目，QWEN 3.6 35B A3B 是一个令人惊叹的模型，甚至量化到 4 位。实际上，我发现它是作为 LLM 支持的单人文本冒险游戏的 GM 的“编写”风格，甚至比一些更快/更笨的前沿模型（如 GPT-5.6-Luna 或 Haiku 4.5）更好，并且它在具有 80k 上下文的 3090 上运行（缓慢）。

因此，当涉及到此类有趣的项目时，我对这些嵌入式 LLM 芯片充满信心。不过，我个人并没有发现我的量化 QWEN 擅长代理任务，而且它喜欢在提示中询问有关文档的问题时胡编乱造。

children.author: Closi
children.textRawHtml:
Scaling is definetly hard - but there is no absolute requirement to put huge flagship models into this technology (although it might be possible over time).

A fairly dumb but FAST model has it's own totally distinct use-cases even if it can't be scaled in size. Think about a LLM-infused-Alexa where the response time is instant. Where you can request it looks at hotel options in Montreal, and it starts answering in half a second rather than a few minutes.

Plus some sort of slow smart + fast dumb combo architectures might also work really well for different classes of problems.
children.textZhHtml:
扩展确实很困难 - 但没有绝对要求将大型旗舰模型放入这项技术中（尽管随着时间的推移可能会实现）。

一个相当愚蠢但快速的模型有它自己完全不同的用例，即使它无法扩展大小。想想一个注入法学硕士的 Alexa，它的响应时间是即时的。您可以在其中请求它查看蒙特利尔的酒店选择，它会在半秒而不是几分钟内开始回答。

加上某种慢速智能+快速愚蠢的组合架构也可能非常适合不同类别的问题。

children.author: formerly_proven
children.textRawHtml: It's quite telling that the 8B Taalas chip was already reticle-sized on TSMC N6. I mean, we're talking about a process that does ~100 MTr/mm², ROM needs about one transistor per bit, but can probably be packed more densely than general logic. Something like, say, 150 megabit/mm² is not a lot. N6 has a 850 mm² reticle limit. This roughly tracks, the article says the chip has 8B parameters and apparently spends about half the area on ROM. There's a reason AI accelerators just use a ton of silicon area (each HBM3 die is >1000mm² of silicon). I imagine this is not terribly viable unless they make it a lot more space efficient e.g. using MLC ROM if they don't already, or use stacked dies with a ROM-optimized process. And then we're back to not cheap, though reticle chips were never in the cheap area to begin with.
children.textZhHtml: 很明显，8B Taalas 芯片在台积电 N6 上已经达到了十字线大小。我的意思是，我们正在讨论的流程约为 100 MTr/mm²，ROM 每位大约需要一个晶体管，但可能可以比一般逻辑封装得更密集。比如说，150 兆位/平方毫米并不是很多。 N6 的十字线限制为 850 mm²。这大致跟踪，文章称该芯片有 8B 参数，并且显然在 ROM 上花费了大约一半的面积。 AI 加速器仅使用大量硅面积（每个 HBM3 芯片的硅面积 >1000mm²）是有原因的。我认为这不是非常可行，除非它们能够提高空间效率，例如使用 MLC ROM（如果尚未使用），或者使用具有 ROM 优化流程的堆叠芯片。然后我们又回到了不便宜的情况，尽管掩模版芯片一开始就不是便宜的区域。

children.author: Tuna-Fish
children.textRawHtml:
Taalas exploits the low cardinality to store one 4-bit weight with one transistor. (They are using metal layer traces for the ROM, and connecting an access transistor to light up one of 16 options.)

Their system is honestly very efficient for the weights, the problem is the KV-cache. That's why HC1 only supports such short context, they use SRAM for that and spend most of what's left of the die for it. The recent advancements that made attention more efficient are probably going to be very useful for them.
children.textZhHtml:
Taalas 利用低基数用一个晶体管存储一个 4 位权重。 （他们为 ROM 使用金属层走线，并连接一个存取晶体管来点亮 16 个选项之一。）

他们的系统对于权重来说确实非常高效，问题在于 KV 缓存。这就是为什么 HC1 只支持如此短的上下文，他们为此使用 SRAM，并为此花费了芯片剩余的大部分内容。最近提高注意力效率的进步可能对他们非常有用。

children.author: phonon
children.textRawHtml: A full wafer like Cerebras is about 60x that, and N2P has about 3x the transistor density. So right now it's technically feasible to etch a 1.4 trillion parameter model.  So roughly DeepSeek-V4-Pro class. Imagine that running a factory, for example.
children.textZhHtml: 像 Cerebras 这样的全晶圆大约是它的 60 倍，而 N2P 的晶体管密度大约是它的 3 倍。所以现在刻蚀1.4万亿参数模型在技术上是可行的。  所以大致是DeepSeek-V4-Pro 类。例如，想象一下经营一家工厂。

children.author: Frannky
children.textRawHtml:
Yes, it also opens up a faster recurring revenue model for hardware companies, faster model obsolescence than how often you change a computer, a server, or a GPU card. I hope they can figure out trillion-parameter models rapidly. Nvidia happened to be the best option for AI after building machines for graphics, so it makes sense they weren't the best idea from scratch for this specific use case. Especially given the scale of the demand and the possibility of recurring revenue, I hope a lot of smart people will try to solve it, compete with each other, and deliver us extremely fast and cheap intelligence.

And one can say LLMs are not as smart as a human, but a lot of the reasoning humans do for product and service generation isn't smart at all—it's just a bit of fuzzy input/output plus some reasoning rules. And then if you hook a robot up to the LLM, you can get results in atoms instead of bits.

I'm very excited about the future. I also hope it will stop money from flowing to bureaucrats who are incentived to keep the problems open to keep the money flowing, and instead facilitate sharing directly with the people (for example, no money to the state to solve homelessness—instead, spay instead with intelligence output to build a house and provide food as part of taxes.)
children.textZhHtml:
是的，它还为硬件公司开辟了一种更快的经常性收入模式，比您更换计算机、服务器或 GPU 卡的频率更快的模型过时速度。我希望他们能够快速找出万亿参数模型。 在构建图形机器之后，Nvidia 恰好是人工智能的最佳选择，因此对于这个特定用例来说，它们并不是从头开始的最佳想法，这是有道理的。特别是考虑到需求的规模和经常性收入的可能性，我希望很多聪明的人会尝试解决它，相互竞争，并为我们提供极其快速和廉价的情报。

人们可以说法学硕士不如人类聪明，但人类为产品和服务生成所做的很多推理根本不聪明——它只是一点模糊的输入/输出加上一些推理规则。然后，如果你将机器人连接到法学硕士，你就可以获得原子而不是比特的结果。

我对未来感到非常兴奋。我还希望它能阻止资金流向那些为了保持资金流动而公开问题的官僚，而是促进直接与人民分享（例如，不向国家提供资金来解决无家可归问题，而是用情报产出来建造房屋并作为税收的一部分提供食物。）
